limitations: The reference is a single physician unblinded post-output reassessment of known development cases.
Reference correction and inclusion of C25 change agreement without changing model behavior.
Higher agreement does not imply better clinical policy on contested OTC/self-care labels.
Rationale quality, clinical outcomes and operational readiness are not established.
The expanded project exceeded the original timebox.

Timing subtype agreement is 31/40 conditional and 38/49 end-to-end. Four refill-policy conflicts and four emergency-versus-same-day disagreements remain unresolved; current GUI retains its original three-bucket contract.
Public repository and presentation disclosures do not establish legal clearance, media permissions, subject consent or a general open-source license.
The first four new GUI checks used the prior dependency build; the final smoke used updated dependencies and supported Node 24.19.0. These are integration observations, not new clinical validation.
The Google Slides-friendly file is an editable PPTX; no native Google Slides copy was created or inspected.

The separate missing-information prompt experiment regressed on the known set (48/50 to 44/50) and was not adopted. Its authored challenge targets are unreviewed AI labels, not physician validation. Independent clinical and prospective evaluation remain pending.

Company-reported physician response times do not establish completed assessment or treatment. The three buckets mix next contact and care setting; urgent-versus-async disagreement alone does not demonstrate harmful delay. A future service-specific reference requires independent clinical approval and a new version.
